data.long_meaning: Shiva, the god of destruction, is the supreme lord who creates, protects and transforms the universe. The name Shivesh means 'God' or 'Lord Shiva'. The name Shivesh carries the meaning “God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shivesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shivesh is a spiritual name that represents the divine presence of Lord Shiva within an individual. It signifies the ultimate reality and the absolute truth.
data.etymology: Shivesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivesh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shivesh carries deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as Lord Shiva is considered one of the primary deities and holds immense importance in the religion. Shiva is associated with several aspects including creation, sustenance, destruction, and transformation. The name is marked with reverence and respect, reflecting the deep-rooted faith and devotion towards Lord Shiva in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shivesh holds profound spiritual significance as it symbolizes the union of the ultimate masculine and feminine energies, symbolized by Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati respectively. The name serves as a constant reminder of the divine connection between these energies that sustains and nourishes the universe. In Hindu spirituality, Lord Shiva is regarded as the embodiment of pure consciousness and self-realization, associated with the ultimate truth and attainment of spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shivesh means the supremely auspicious and divine one, who is Shiva himself. It represents the purest form of consciousness and the ultimate reality.

historical_references.reference: Shiva was known as 'Mahadeva' or 'Great God' and 'Rudra' or 'Howler', representing the aspect of destruction. Later, he came to be known as 'Shiva', the auspicious one.
historical_references.context: During the Vedic period, Shiva was one of the principal deities. He was depicted as a destructive force, but also as the god of regeneration and fertility.

historical_references.reference: During the medieval period, the Hindu temple architecture reached its culmination in the form of the 'Shivalinga' or the phallic representation of Shiva.
historical_references.context: The Shivalinga was considered the symbolic representation of the deity, believed to house the divine presence of Shiva.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivesh' is of Hindu origin and translates to 'Supreme Lord Shiva'. In modern context, this name is often associated with spirituality, meditation, and self-improvement. On Instagram, one can find numerous accounts dedicated to Shiva and his teachings, with visual content showcasing various forms of the deity, mantras, and meditation techniques. On YouTube, there are numerous channels and videos offering insights into the philosophy of Shiva and his role in Hinduism. Reddit, a popular social media platform, has several subreddits dedicated to Hinduism and Shiva, where users discuss various aspects of the deity and his significance. These platforms have enabled individuals to explore and connect with the spiritual practices and teachings associated with Shiva, regardless of geographical location or physical assembly.
